html:
The Miwok are four related Indigenous peoples of Northern and Central California, living around San Francisco Bay, in the Sacramento Valley and in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada. They spoke Miwok languages of the Utian family.

The four groups were the Coast Miwok, the Lake Miwok, the Bay Miwok and the Plains and Sierra Miwok. Like their neighbours the Pomo, Ohlone and Yokuts, they lived in villages and ate acorns, salmon, seeds and game.

In 1579 Francis Drake probably landed among the Coast Miwok north of the Golden Gate. From the 1770s many Bay and Coast Miwok were drawn into the Spanish missions. In 1848 the Gold Rush began in Sierra Miwok country and brought miners, violence and hunger. The people of Yosemite Valley were partly Miwok.
sum: The Miwok are four related Indigenous peoples of Northern and Central California, living around San Francisco Bay, in the Sacramento Valley and in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada. They spoke Miwok languages of the Utian family.
